# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Datasec/NexusAI RD-322 + RD-323, TIER 2, two subjects) | **RD-322 GO · RD-323 GO-with-findings — and its Major is the THIRD check-that-cannot-fail of the night, inside the change built to stop that family.** `healthSweeper.runOnce` sets `p1 = p1s.length` filtering `verdict.startsWith('P1')`, **which includes `'P1-degraded'`, so `p1 >= degraded` always** — and the override fails the tick on it, **four lines below its own comment promising that degraded is deliberately NOT failure.** Measured against the SHIPPED class with a real stub. **And the cell certifying the carve-out asserts `f({degraded:1, p1:0}) === false` — a shape `runOnce` CANNOT PRODUCE**: a green, always-running assertion over an unreachable state. Its phrase: *'same defect family as RD-322, one file along.'* **Enumerated every consumer over a stated frame** — 12 schedulers, 35 return shapes, old predicate vs each scheduler's own `_failed` **evaluated by execution on all 35** — 8 verdicts changed, 8 of 9 intended, **25 adversarial shapes with no false positive**, and the contract confirmed in BOTH directions. | **1.0** | On RD-322 it added **an arm the ticket did not have** (delete the record so `blocked` goes true for the WRONG reason — the cell still reddens, so narrow rather than vacuous), and **verified BOTH grounds of the builder's RED-over-skip disposition itself across the WHOLE `.github` tree** (5 workflows, 6 `runs-on` all ubuntu-latest, zero `container:`, zero matrix legs, zero self-hosted, Dockerfile user `node`, no git hooks). Re-ran the red-proof at the FULL-SUITE frame so entanglement would show: M2 **exactly 1 red across 2171 cells**; M3 measured **15, not the claimed 13** — the two extra are pre-existing controls from two OLDER suites, so **the difference runs in the change's favour** and the 13 was merely over an unnamed narrower frame. Counts re-derived by name-diffing at three SHAs. |
| QA agent (fleet, Datasec/NexusAI TWO MOVED HEADS `731aa6e` + `690bed9`, TIER 2) | **GO-with-findings on both — and it answered the exact question a rewrite invites: the AST guard MISSES what the regex caught.** G-1: three additive in-frame shapes bypass the stamp — a `writeFileSync` with a template literal, with a string literal, and a spread carrying the key. **T-A8b passes the entire file 33/33 while its matched pair T-MB2 (identical hazard, object literal) is RED — the only variable is SERIALISATION.** *'The fixes-one-blindness-opens-another case by name.'* **G-2 is the finding of the night: it ruled the retained `stripComments()` load-bearing and its stated reason FALSE TWICE — a URL can hide what those cells count, AND the live damage needs no URL at all.** Two ordinary prose comments contain `/*` (`server.js:638`, `:1097`), each opening a bogus block: measured against acorn's own comment ranges, **31,845 non-comment characters deleted across 116 ranges, lines 638-713 and 1097-2062 gone — ~1,040 lines.** Proved with a byte-identical payload in three placements (outside the hole RED, inside GREEN, URL-on-line GREEN) — **and `THE BUG` is a `not.toMatch`, so deleting text makes it PASS: it fails OPEN.** | **1.0** | **Its fairness is what makes it usable:** it stated plainly that no current deciding site sits in a deleted span, the WIRING patterns count identically today, the cells are byte-unchanged — **so no live defect and NOT a regression; what is wrong is the DECISION RECORDED in the commit.** Re-derived the builder's '256 computed assignments' over **three named frames** (239 guard-frame / 256 all-tracked / 145 backend) — it reproduces exactly,
